subject.title: [Feature]: Native E2EE Browser Chat, No Third-Party Required

question: Should OpenClaw pursue native no-third-party browser-held E2EE chat as a core Gateway/WebChat capability, define Gateway/plugin seams for an external encrypted browser transport first, or defer this direction?
rationale: Current chat semantics expose message text to the Gateway, and the request changes encryption, browser/device trust, transcript storage, routing isolation, relay fallback, and core-versus-plugin ownership boundaries that automation cannot safely choose.

options.title: Approve Design-First Gateway Capability
options.body: Define the threat model, encrypted envelope protocol, browser-held key lifecycle, transcript semantics, and Gateway/Control UI contracts before implementation.

options.title: Make It Plugin-First
options.body: Keep core lean by adding only the missing Gateway/plugin SDK seams needed for an external encrypted browser transport to integrate safely.

options.title: Defer Native Transport
options.body: Keep WebChat, Tailscale, Matrix E2EE, Signal, and dmScope isolation as supported paths until maintainers sponsor a native encrypted browser transport.

recommendation.title: Approve Design-First Gateway Capability
recommendation.body: Define the threat model, encrypted envelope protocol, browser-held key lifecycle, transcript semantics, and Gateway/Control UI contracts before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The blocking choice is primarily an encryption/key ownership and transcript visibility boundary, with WebChat product ownership following after the security model is accepted.
